item.title: Cypress Hill Embrace Latin Roots on First All-Spanish Album ‘Dios Bendiga’: ‘It’s a Prayer for the Culture’
item.description:
Here's a short, engaging podcast script based on the article:
[Intro music fades out]
Host: Welcome to "Trending on Billboard"! Today, we're shining the spotlight on hip-hop legends Cypress Hill. With a career spanning over three decades, this iconic group has left an indelible mark on the music scene.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: Formed in the early '90s, Cypress Hill - consisting of B-Real, Sen Dog, DJ Muggs, and later Eric Bobo - captured the harsh social reality of California and Los Angeles, blending innovative sounds with a strong Latino identity. This connection to their roots was solidified in 1999 with the release of "Los Grandes Éxitos en Español", a project that featured iconic songs adapted into Spanish.
[Short music transition]
Host: Fast forward to today, Cypress Hill is releasing their first album of entirely original Spanish-language material, "Dios Bendiga". This project aims to reclaim the cultural heritage that has been with the group since day one. As B-Real tells Billboard Argentina, "Dios Bendiga is more than just a collection of songs; it's a prayer for the culture... our heritage isn't a trend, but a divine legacy and a global future."
[Short music transition]
Host: The album features a collaboration with Argentine artist Trueno on the track "Saca la Bolsita", adding a local flavor to the project. Sen Dog praises Trueno, saying "he's a student of hip-hop - someone who's great to work with."
[Soft music continues to play]
Host: Cypress Hill's influence extends far beyond their connection to Latin culture. With seven songs on the Billboard Hot 100, including the iconic "Insane in the Brain", which hit No. 19 in 1993, they've cemented their legacy as one of the most innovative and successful acts of the '90s. And with millions of records sold, they've paved the way for Latino artists to make their mark in the U.S. hip-hop scene.
[Outro music starts playing]
Host: That's it for today's episode of "Trending on Billboard". Cypress Hill's new album "Dios Bendiga" is out now, and they'll be performing live in Buenos Aires on November 8th. Thanks for tuning in!
[Outro music continues to play until the end]
